query: Técnicas de preprocesamiento y clasificación para mejorar el pronóstico de irradiancia solar Explorar métodos de preprocesamiento como lógica difusa, clustering y clasificación de datos que contribuyen a mejorar la calidad de los datos de entrada y la precisión de los modelos de pronóstico. El preprocesamiento con lógica difusa permite manejar la incertidumbre y variabilidad rápida en variables meteorológicas, mejorando la precisión en pronósticos a muy corto plazo. La clasificación y clustering de datos meteorológicos según condiciones climáticas facilita la adaptación de modelos a diferentes escenarios, incrementando la exactitud del pronóstico. El uso de modelos híbridos que integran preprocesamiento avanzado con redes neuronales y machine learning tradicional ha demostrado mejoras cuantificables en métricas de error. Estas técnicas son especialmente útiles para manejar la intermitencia y variabilidad de la irradiancia solar en regiones con alta nubosidad o condiciones atmosféricas complejas. Descripción de técnicas de preprocesamiento y clasificación. Resultados cuantitativos que evidencien mejoras en precisión. Análisis de casos con alta variabilidad atmosférica. Limitaciones y propuestas de mejora en preprocesamiento.

This method is aimed to correctly classify the sky and actual cloud pixels in the vicinity of the sun. As a result of the classification, pixels with classes different from the K-means class located in the sun center are deleted and labeled as the sky. Thus, the classification of pixels around the sun that are incorrectly classified as clouds due to brightness are corrected as the sky. Pixels located in the center of the sun and having the same class as the K-means class are classified according to whether they are detected as the sun or not. If the relevant pixel is classified as a sun pixel during the sun clas­ sification stage, it remains a sun pixel; if not, it is classified as a cloud pixel. In this way, the sun, cloud, and sky classes around the sun can be determined more accurately. 2.4. Cloud motion forecasting

Therefore, the development of successful solar radiation fore­ casting methods has become an essential element for increasing solar energy use and grid integration [5]. Different solar radiation forecasting methodologies have been pro­ posed for various time periods in the literature. Numerical weather prediction (NWP) [6–8] or satellite-based forecast models [9], Aguiar, Pereira [10], Alonso-Montesinos and Batlles [11] are common among these methods and approaches. Using related methods, successful fore­ casting’s are made for large areas and long-time scales. However, esti­ mates on these area and time scales are insufficient to provide information about high-frequency solar radiation fluctuations due to their coverage of large areas and long periods. For example, while the general area of a given region is predicted to have a sunny day, sunlight may be interrupted from time to time by cloud cover. These in­ terruptions may affect the energy production level of any solar power plant installed in that region. Therefore, shorter-term, precise site-specific, and on-site forecasts are needed compared to NWP or

Linear statistical models such as autoregressive (AR) and autoregressive moving average (ARMA) that uses realtime measurement data have been successfully applied for short-term forecasting [8], [9]. Auto-Regressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model which combines the autoregressive component to a moving average (MA) is also widely researched for application in solar forecasting. In these linear models, the relationship between the input variables and the forecasted variable are derived through statistical analysis. However, non-linear characteristics caused by variation in weather including cloud cover and atmospheric particulates further complicates the short-term forecasting [10]. Artificial intelligence or machine learning techniques are widely researched as an alternative solution for estimating processes associated with non-linear functions. In [11], artificial neural network (ANN) is used for shortterm solar forecasting based on multiple input variable such as temperature, humidity, pressure and wind.
